subject: sr-maths
title: Model Question Paper 2
meta: Time: 3 hours · Maximum marks: 100 · Modelled on the April 2026 NIOS paper
instructions: All questions are compulsory. Where a question has OR, answer either one.
Section A: questions 1–20 are MCQs (1 mark each); 21–24 have two 1-mark parts; 25–28 have four 1-mark parts; 29 has six 1-mark parts.
Section B: questions 30–38 carry 2 marks, 39–43 carry 4 marks and 44–45 carry 6 marks.
Every answer shows the working. Questions from previous NIOS papers show the exam they appeared in.

sections.title: Objective type questions of four 1-mark parts.

questions.q: For the line 3x − 4y + 12 = 0 find: (a) its slope; (b) its x-intercept; (c) its y-intercept; (d) its distance from the origin.

True or False: (a) Two matrices are comparable if they have the same number of rows and columns. (b) If A is skew-symmetric, all its diagonal elements are zero. (c) (AB)' = A'B'. (d) If A = [[2, −1, 5], [3, 8, 7]], then A' = [[2, 3], [−1, 8], [5, 7]].
questions.answer:
(a) True.
(b) True — aᵢᵢ = −aᵢᵢ ⇒ aᵢᵢ = 0.
(c) False — (AB)' = B'A'.
(d) True — rows become columns.

questions.q: Answer: (i) What are xi, yj, zk called for r = xi + yj + zk? (ii) If |OA| = 4, |OB| = 5, |OC| = 6 along the axes, express OP. (iii) The centroid of ΔABC with position vectors a, b, c? (iv) The point dividing AB internally in 2 : 3?
questions.answer:
(i) The component vectors of r along the axes.
(ii) OP = 4i + 5j + 6k.
(iii) (a + b + c)/3.
(iv) (2b + 3a)/(2 + 3) = (3a + 2b)/5.

questions.q: (a) Negate: '√5 is not a rational number.' (b) Converse of 'If x is a prime number, then x is even.' (c) Contrapositive of 'If a number is odd, then its square is not negative.' (d) Combine with 'if and only if': P: if two angles of a triangle are equal, it is isosceles; Q: if a triangle is isosceles, two of its angles are equal.
questions.answer:
(a) √5 is a rational number.
(b) If x is even, then x is a prime number.
(c) If the square of a number is negative, then the number is not odd.
(d) A triangle is isosceles if and only if two of its angles are equal.

sections.title: Objective type question of six 1-mark parts.

questions.q: a = i + j + k and b = i − j + k. (a) Find a × b. (b) Find the angle between a and b. (c) Find the projection of a on b. (d) Is a × b = b × a? (e) Find the area of the parallelogram with a and b as diagonals. (f) Check whether |a × b|² = |a|²|b|² − (a·b)².
Find the area of the triangle whose vertices are (1, 2), (−2, 3) and (−3, −4).
Find the angle between the x-axis and the line joining (5, 4) and (6, 3).
Solve x dy/dx + 2y = x².
questions.answer:
dy/dx + (2/x)y = x. IF = e^(∫2/x dx) = x².
yx² = ∫x·x² dx = x⁴/4 + C ⇒ y = x²/4 + C/x².

questions.answer:
Maximise Z = 40x + 70y
subject to 2x + 3y ≤ 30, x ≥ 0, y ≥ 0.

questions.q: Write the converse and contrapositive of 'If a triangle is equilateral, then it is isosceles'.
questions.answer:
Converse: if a triangle is isosceles, then it is equilateral (false in general).
Contrapositive: if a triangle is not isosceles, then it is not equilateral (true, equivalent to the original).

questions.q: The vertices of ΔABC are A(−3, 3), B(5, −2) and C(−1, −4). If M and N are the midpoints of AB and AC, show that MN = ½BC.
The eccentricity of an ellipse is 5/8 and the distance between its foci is 10. Find the length of its latus rectum.
Using elementary column transformations, find the inverse of A = [[2, −6], [1, −2]].
f(x) = (1 − cos 4x)/x² for x < 0, a for x = 0, √x/(√(16 + √x) − 4) for x > 0. If f is continuous at 0, find a.
questions.answer:
LHL: 1 − cos 4x = 2 sin²2x ⇒ 2 sin²2x/x² = 8[sin 2x/(2x)]² → 8.
RHL: rationalise: √x(√(16 + √x) + 4)/(16 + √x − 16) = √(16 + √x) + 4 → 4 + 4 = 8.
Continuity: a = 8.

questions.q: Find the angle between the line x − 2y + z = 0 = x + 2y − 2z and the line (x − 1)/3 = (1 − y)/1 = z/0.
Using properties of determinants, prove |a−b−c 2a 2a; 2b b−c−a 2b; 2c 2c c−a−b| = (a + b + c)³.
questions.answer:
R₁ → R₁ + R₂ + R₃: R₁ becomes (a + b + c, a + b + c, a + b + c). Take (a + b + c) out:
Δ = (a + b + c)|1 1 1; 2b b−c−a 2b; 2c 2c c−a−b|.
C₂ → C₂ − C₁, C₃ → C₃ − C₁: |1 0 0; 2b −(a+b+c) 0; 2c 0 −(a+b+c)|.
Expand along R₁: (a + b + c) × (a + b + c)² = (a + b + c)³.

questions.q: Verify Lagrange's mean value theorem for f(x) = (x − 1)(x − 2)(x − 3) on [0, 4].
questions.answer:
f is a polynomial, so it is continuous on [0, 4] and differentiable on (0, 4).
f(0) = −6, f(4) = 6 ⇒ [f(4) − f(0)]/(4 − 0) = 12/4 = 3.
f(x) = x³ − 6x² + 11x − 6 ⇒ f'(x) = 3x² − 12x + 11.
3c² − 12c + 11 = 3 ⇒ 3c² − 12c + 8 = 0 ⇒ c = 2 ± 2/√3 ≈ 3.15 or 0.85, both in (0, 4).
Hence the theorem is verified.

or.q: Verify Rolle's theorem for f(x) = x(x − 1)(x − 2) on [0, 2].
or.answer:
Polynomial ⇒ continuous and differentiable. f(0) = f(2) = 0.
f(x) = x³ − 3x² + 2x ⇒ f'(x) = 3x² − 6x + 2 = 0 ⇒ c = 1 ± 1/√3 ≈ 1.58 or 0.42, both in (0, 2).
Verified.
